halcyon.lastTransmission: We found something… near the delta… it changes everything—

photos.label: Mum and Dad
photos.caption: Their porch, the summer you got the job

photos.label: Your sister
photos.caption: Her graduation, you in the back row

prelaunch.brief: Three years ago Halcyon-1 landed in Jezero Crater and went silent. You are going after them.
prelaunch.briefAfter: Before you go, choose the photo you will carry and write a message for home.
prelaunch.messagePlaceholder: Write a message home. It will be sent when you launch.
prelaunch.defaultMessage: I'll be home before you know it.
prelaunch.crewLabel: Halcyon-1 crew, silent for three years
prelaunch.photoHint: It goes in your pocket. It comes with you to Mars. Use ← → or 1 2 3.
prelaunch.messageHint: Your message is sent when you launch. Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.

go.text: All stations GO. You are cleared for launch.

liftoff.text: Liftoff. You'll feel the whole ship push you into your seat. That is thrust, and it is working.

maxq.text: Max-Q. The air is pushing hardest on your ship right now. Hold steady, it eases in a few seconds.

orbit.text: Orbit achieved. Nothing is holding you up but speed. You are falling around the Earth, and missing it.

transfer.text: Transfer burn complete. You are coasting to Mars on a path the Sun's gravity bends. Use time warp, but stay alert.

entry.text: Entry interface. Our signal is eleven minutes old by the time you read this, so the next seven minutes are yours alone.

afterBlackout.text: …copy, we have you. Chute is out.

landed.text: Touchdown confirmed. We heard it eleven minutes after you did. Welcome to Jezero. Suit up when you're ready.

firstEva.text: Halcyon-1's lander should be about 170 metres north-west of you. First: scan the ground and get power running. Then go find them.

scan.text: Scan data received. The radar shows layers under you: this crater floor was once the bottom of a lake.

energy.text: Panels are up and the ice is mapped. With that, the ship can make oxygen and methane for the trip home.

sample.text: Sample sealed and logged. Every kilogram you carry costs fuel on the way home, so choose well.

logPickup.text: You found one of their logs. Bring it to the comms console in the ship and upload it.

log.text: Log received. We're listening to it now. Thank you for bringing them back to us.

discovery.text: We're seeing the same patterns they did. It's not proof of life. But it's the best clue anyone has ever found. Upload everything.

complete.text: That's all of it. The return window won't wait. Get to the pilot seat and come home.

paleBlueDot.text: Look up, just above the crater rim. That bright point of light is Earth. Everyone you have ever loved is on that dot.

family1.text: The house is quiet without you. We watched the launch four times. Eat something that isn't from a pouch for us when you're back.

family2.text: They showed your landing on the news. I didn't understand half of it. I understood that you made it. That's enough.

log1.title: Halcyon-1 · personal log · Mei Lin Hart · sol 41
log1.text: Forty-one sols. Tomas has started talking to the plants. I've started answering for them. The delta is everything we hoped: layers on layers, a whole lake written in stone. Elena says we stay on schedule. I keep looking north-east anyway.

log2.title: Halcyon-1 · mission log · Elena Marsh · sol 97
log2.text: HQ forecasts a regional dust storm in three to five sols. Mei Lin found something in the delta she can't explain: dark rims, pale centres, like spots on a leopard. If it's what she thinks, it changes everything. One more trip. We'll be back before the storm.

final.title: Halcyon-1 · final log · Elena Marsh · sol 99
final.text: The storm came early. The panels are buried and the batteries are going. HQ told us to stay inside. I said yes, and then I said one more trip, because it mattered so much. It still matters. But a warning is not an obstacle. Whoever comes after us: listen to it. And finish the work.

returnTrip.caption: Trans-Earth injection: the engine burns for home
Cruise: seven months between two worlds
Earth entry at 11.5 km/s, faster than any Mars entry

homecoming.title: Homecoming
homecoming.text: You were away 2 years, 7 months. The world saw what you found in the delta, and the names of the Halcyon-1 crew were read out at the start of the evening news.
homecoming.family: You came home. That's the whole message. You came home.

adrift.title: Adrift: The Last Message
adrift.text: There was not enough fuel to come back.

rud.title: Rapid Unscheduled Disassembly
rud.text: Engineers have a polite phrase for when a rocket explodes. This was a very rapid, very unscheduled disassembly. The good news: the black box survived.

burnup.title: Burn-up
burnup.text: Entering an atmosphere at thousands of metres per second turns air into plasma hotter than the surface of the Sun. Without enough protection, nothing survives it.

outOfBreath.title: Out of Breath
outOfBreath.text: The suit is a tiny spaceship, and its air ran out before you got home. On Mars, every step outside is measured against the gauge on your wrist.

bankrupt.title: Bankrupt
bankrupt.text: The agency has been sold to a company that makes self-heating soup. Your rocket now stands in a museum lobby, next to a sign that says PLEASE DO NOT CLIMB. You get to start over with fresh funding.

coldMorning.title: Cold Morning
coldMorning.text: It was below freezing on the pad. The cheap seals went stiff, and hot gas found its way through. The warning was on the screen, and the launch went ahead anyway.

theFoam.title: The Foam
theFoam.text: Something hit the heat shield on the way up. It looked small. Nobody inspected it. On entry, the plasma found the damage.

pureOxygen.title: Pure Oxygen
pureOxygen.text: In pure oxygen, a single spark becomes a fire that spreads faster than anyone can react.

successfulFailure.title: Successful Failure
successfulFailure.text: A tank exploded halfway to Mars. You stayed calm, worked the problem, and came home alive. The mission failed. You didn't.

silentReturn.title: Silent Return
silentReturn.text: The capsule lost its air on the way down, and nobody was wearing a suit. It landed perfectly, and silently.

unitError.title: Unit Error
unitError.text: One supplier's numbers were in pound-force, everyone else's in newtons. The ship flew exactly as its maths said, into the ground.

falseTouchdown.title: False Touchdown
falseTouchdown.text: A cheap sensor felt the legs unfold and decided you had landed. The engine shut off forty metres up.

spin.title: Spin
spin.text: A thruster stuck open and the ship spun faster and faster. You found the right switches before your vision went grey, and survived.

beagle.title: Beagle
beagle.text: You landed perfectly. Then the panels never fully opened, and they covered the antenna. Nobody on Earth ever heard from you.

hq.text: We've run every number we have, three times, with every team. There's no rescue we can fly in time. We are so sorry. We're staying on this channel.

tries: You run the numbers again. Fuel: 0 kg. The answer doesn't change.
You try to point the ship back toward home. Nothing pushes it there.
You recheck every valve and every tank. Empty is still empty.
You call HQ again. The reply will take minutes. You already know what it says.
adrift.dim: The lights dim to save power.
adrift.photo: You take out the photo you chose before launch.
adrift.reply: The reply from your family arrived 14 minutes later.
adrift.replyText: We got your message. We're all here, together, reading it again and again. We love you. We are so proud of you. Come home to us if you can.
adrift.help: If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available: findahelpline.com

challenger.title: Challenger, 1986
challenger.text: On 28 January 1986 it was about 2 °C at the launch pad. Engineers warned the night before that the rubber O-rings sealing the solid rocket boosters might not seal in the cold. The launch went ahead. 73 seconds after liftoff a seal failed and Challenger broke apart. All seven crew died.
challenger.lesson: Listen to warnings. Don't let risk become normal.

columbia.title: Columbia, 2003
columbia.text: 82 seconds after launch, a piece of foam struck the leading edge of Columbia's left wing. The damage was never inspected in orbit. On re-entry on 1 February 2003, hot gas entered the wing and the shuttle broke apart. All seven crew died.
columbia.lesson: Small damage can kill. Inspect it.

apollo1.title: Apollo 1, 1967
apollo1.text: On 27 January 1967, during a ground test, a fire started in the pure-oxygen cabin of Apollo 1. It spread in seconds. Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died.
apollo1.lesson: Fires in oxygen-rich air spread terrifyingly fast.

apollo13.title: Apollo 13, 1970
apollo13.text: Two days into the flight, an oxygen tank exploded. The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat while engineers on the ground worked out how to bring them home. All three came back alive.

soyuz11.title: Soyuz 11, 1971
soyuz11.text: On 30 June 1971 a valve opened as the Soyuz 11 modules separated before re-entry, and the cabin lost its air. The crew wore no pressure suits. Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov and Viktor Patsayev are the only people to have died in space.
soyuz11.lesson: Wear the suit in critical phases.

marsClimateOrbiter.title: Mars Climate Orbiter, 1999
marsClimateOrbiter.text: Ground software gave thruster data in pound-force seconds, while the navigation team expected newton-seconds. The small error grew over months, and in September 1999 the orbiter flew far too low into Mars' atmosphere and was lost.

marsPolarLander.title: Mars Polar Lander, 1999
marsPolarLander.text: Its legs most likely jolted when they unfolded, a sensor read that as touchdown, and the engine shut off about 40 m up. In 2016 ESA's Schiaparelli lander also cut its descent short after a sensor gave a false reading.

gemini8.title: Gemini 8, 1966
gemini8.text: A thruster stuck on and spun the capsule to about one turn per second. Neil Armstrong shut down the main thrusters and used the re-entry thrusters to stop the spin. The crew came home safely.
gemini8.lesson: Stay calm and know your controls.

beagle2.title: Beagle 2, 2003
beagle2.text: Beagle 2 landed on Mars on Christmas Day 2003 and was never heard from. In 2015 orbital photos found it on the surface: its solar panels had only partly opened, covering the antenna.
beagle2.lesson: Success can still fail at the last step.
